text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty triggered: P0 - us-west-2a (az1a) inference latency spike and TCP econnreset increase. Alert: inferer-5xx-rate > 8% and p95 latency > 800ms for last 5m. PD: PD12345.

sara (oncall): seeing the same in the grafana dashboard. p95 tokens shot from 120ms -> 900ms. Rolling canaries failing healthchecks.

mike: can someone dump the nginx+proxy logs for a failing host? suspicious of network jitter.

ops_lead: quick checklist: 1) confirm host-level NIC errors 2) confirm ENI attach/spill events 3) check AZ capacity from EC2 console 4) route traffic to other AZs if healthy.

eng-runtime: running `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide` shows several pods on i-0a1b2c3d stuck in `CrashLoopBackOff` with socket errors in logs. snippet: ```2026-03-15T12:05:02Z inference-server ERROR: connection reset by peer (EPIPE) while streaming```.

infra: AWS events show a burst of `AttachNetworkInterface` throttles and `INSUFFICIENT_INSTANCE_CAPACITY` for g5 instances in az1a in the last 20m. Also seeing increased `EC2 - Instance ID: i-0a1b2c3d` - `ENI RX dropped` counters.

cs-rep: we have a few 1st-party customers reporting higher latencies and a small number of API 500s. I'm drafting a notice but holding until we have impact numbers.

sara (oncall): can we flip the AZ circuit breaker and steer inference traffic off az1a? what's the status of cross-zone routing?

eng-runtime: starting immediate routing policy change: will set routing weight for az1a -> 0 and enable fallback to the regional pool (az1b/c). Command: ```rbctl route update --region us-west-2 --policy az-weight --az az1a=0,az1b=60,az1c=40 --dry-run=false``` will push now. Expect minimal client interruption (sticky sessions may see drops).

incident-bot: deploy-bot: `route-update` job queued by eng-runtime. Job id: job-789.

infra: PSR (platform status) shows we still have some capacity pressure in az1a. AWS console listing shows a partial network plane degradation — multiple hosts reporting kernel-level rx-queue drops. AWS is investigating.

mike: rolling a manual drain of pods on the worst hosts to avoid sticky KV cache being lost mid-request. `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data <node>` then reschedule to other AZ nodes. Doing in small batches.

eng-runtime: canaries are re-running. first set shows significantly reduced 5xx after route update, p95 back to ~200ms in az1b/c. Some in-flight requests failed but service stabilized.

cs-rep: accepted — sending initial customer notice: "We experienced elevated latency and some request failures in us-west-2a starting 12:05 UTC. Traffic has been routed away from the affected AZ and mitigation is in progress. We'll follow up with details."

ops_lead: handoff plan: sara, you'll own active mitigation until 13:30 UTC, then ops_lead will take over for postmortem orchestration. Make sure to capture the exact nodes impacted.

sara (oncall): acknowledged, I'll keep monitoring. setting a short-term autoscaling cushion for inference pool to absorb extra load in az1b/c: `asctl scale --pool inference-regional --buffer 20%`

infra: FYI AWS support case opened: #CASE-987654321. They report a known internal networking event in the AZ causing NIC RX queue saturation on some instance types. No ETA yet.

mike: added circuit-breaker in the proxy layer to fail fast for connections with >2 retransmits. Config snippet: ```proxy.conf: connection_retries: 2; fast_fail_threshold: 3``` should reduce tail latency and reduce retries. Rolling update to proxies in 5m.

eng-runtime: log snippet from a problematic host: ```tcp_receive_queue: drops=1420, rx_errors=87, tx_errors=0; dmesg: 'net_ratelimit: NIC hw rx drop'``` suggests driver/hw-level drops not application.

sara (oncall): monitoring customer error charts — impact concentrated on a subset of customers with sticky sessions pinned to az1a. Recommending we invalidate sticky tokens for those customers as part of remediation. CS to coordinate messaging.

cs-rep: I'll contact top-5 affected accounts directly. Draft in #support-desk for review.

ops_lead: temporary mitigation summary: 1) routing weight az1a->0 (complete) 2) proxy circuit-breaker enabled 3) drained worst nodes 4) autoscale buffer + reschedule 5) AWS case open. Next: confirm no data loss in KV caches, gather perf traces, and prepare incident report.

incident-bot: NOTE: PagerDuty updated - incident severity remains P1 while mitigation continues.

eng-runtime: verifying KV cache consistency — small cache warm-up expected, but no persistent data loss observed. Will instrument longer-term cache replication detection.

sara (oncall): handing off to ops_lead at 13:30 UTC as planned. ops_lead, take watchers and update incident channel. I'll post the timeline up to my handoff.

ops_lead: taking over. I'll coordinate with infra for root cause once AWS provides logs. Preparing a postmortem template and assigning action items: deeper ENI metrics, retry strategy, cross-AZ session draining improvements, and better canarying for network churn.

mike: suggest we add a runbook step to proactively reweight traffic when EC2 `ENI RX dropped` crosses threshold X for >5m.

infra: AWS updated support case: they attribute to "host NIC buffer pressure due to hypervisor network plane grooming" — they provided host level logs and are recommending instance replacement in az1a. They've scheduled a rolling host replacement window.

eng-runtime: queued node replacements and will prefer heterogenous instance spread to avoid capacity shortages if az returns flakey. Also adding telemetry: emit `eni_rx_drop` metric at 10s granularity to alert earlier.

cs-rep: customer notice sent and updated. No escalations to legal yet.

ops_lead: closing action checklist for immediate mitigation. We'll keep routing weight at az1a=0 until AWS confirms resolved and we see sustained healthy metrics for 30m post-restore. Assigning follow-ups to eng-runtime/infra for remediation tasks.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigated (traffic rerouted). Status: MONITORING. PD: PD12345.

ops_lead: final note for timeline: root cause likely AZ-level network plane degradation causing ENI RX queue saturation on some instance types, leading to econnreset and increased latency. Postmortem to follow with RCA and preventive actions.

sara (oncall): thanks everyone. I'll compile notes and handoff doc into the incident tracker.

mike: leaving some logs/commands here for the postmortem: `aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=availability-zone,Values=us-west-2a --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].{ID:InstanceId,State:State.Name,InstanceType:InstanceType}'` and `sudo ethtool -S eth0 | grep rx-`

ops_lead: closing the channel for active mitigation. Keep watchers if AWS posts updates. PD incident will remain open until remediation is validated.

incident-bot: Incident PD12345 status changed: RESOLVED -> MONITORING.
